extracted.intended_audience: federal regulators, fisheries managers, foreign governments seeking MMPA comparability findings, environmental lawyers and NGOs
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating whether a foreign harvesting nation's regulatory program for specified fisheries is 'comparable in effectiveness' to the United States' regulatory program under the Marine Mammal Protection Act (MMPA), and documenting/issuing formal comparability findings that permit or restrict importation of fish and fish products. Includes use of documentary evidence, court remand compliance, and application of the Final Rule procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparability finding: meet applicable Final Rule conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A comparability finding means that each of the harvesting nation's Export and/or Exempt fisheries covered by the finding meet the applicable conditions specified in the Final Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 50 CFR 216.24(h)(6) and (h)(7). A comparability finding becomes valid upon publication in the Federal Register (50 CFR 216.24(h)(8)(i) and (iv)). NMFS evaluates whether fisheries meet the Final Rule's conditions before issuing a finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable proof requirement under MMPA (16 U.S.C. 1371(a)(2)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of applying the import ban, the Secretary of Commerce shall insist on reasonable proof from the government of any nation from which fish or fish products will be exported to the United States of the effects on ocean mammals of the commercial fishing technology in use for such fish or fish products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reasonable proof is not provided, the MMPA requires banning importation of commercial fish or fish products caught with technology resulting in incidental kill or serious injury of ocean mammals in excess of U.S. standards (16 U.S.C. 1371(a)(2)). Documentary submissions from the exporting government are a central source of this proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary-evidence basis for findings
rubrics_metrics.description: NMFS bases the comparability findings on documentary evidence submitted by the harvesting nation's government and other relevant, readily available information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency must evaluate documentary evidence provided by the foreign government and other public information; determinations must be supported by that evidence and described in NMFS' Decision Memorandum (e.g., NMFS' Decision Memorandum dated March 2, 2026).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparability in effectiveness to U.S. regulatory program
rubrics_metrics.description: The foreign government's regulatory program for specified fisheries must be comparable in effectiveness to the United States' regulatory program under the MMPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparability assessment focuses on the foreign program's regulation of incidental and intentional mortality and serious injury of marine mammals in fisheries. NMFS concluded GNZ's regulatory program for specified set net and trawl fisheries is comparable in effectiveness to U.S. program based on reviewed evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species- and fishery-specific effects must be addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluations must consider the effects of the specified fisheries on particular marine mammal species (e.g., Hector's dolphins, Māui dolphins) and other potentially affected marine mammals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Litigation challenged NMFS for not adequately addressing effects on specific species; NMFS must address those concerns in its analysis and Decision Memorandum when assessing comparability for individual fishery IDs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate explanation and evidentiary support (APA standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: NMFS must adequately explain its rationale and support its determinations with documentary evidence; failure to do so can render a decision arbitrary and capricious under the Administrative Procedure Act (APA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The U.S. Court of International Trade vacated and remanded NMFS' 2024 decision because the agency's rationale was inconsistent with the MMPA and it failed to adequately explain and support determinations with documentary evidence. Analyses must be consistent with the MMPA and fully explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand and discretionary review procedures (50 CFR 216.24(h)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: NMFS may conduct discretionary review pursuant to 50 CFR 216.24(h)(8)(vii) and must respond to court remands by issuing remand comparability findings within court-ordered timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NMFS conducted a discretionary review of prior findings and filed remand comparability findings with the court on January 6, 2026, per court instructions. Agency must incorporate supplemental information obtained during remand and explain any changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal validity of comparability findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparability findings are valid and in effect from the date specified in the Notice through the stated period or for such other period as NMFS may specify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Notice states the findings are valid and in effect from March 11, 2026 through December 31, 2029, or for such other period as NMFS may specify. Publication in the Federal Register makes the finding effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Rule process established in 2016 for evaluating harvesting nations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Rule (81 FR 54390; August 15, 2016) established a process to evaluate a harvesting nation's regulatory program concerning incidental and intentional mortality and serious injury of marine mammals for purposes of import control under section 1371(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NMFS applies the procedures and conditions set out in the Final Rule when evaluating comparability; see the Final Rule and accompanying Federal Register notices (e.g., 90 FR 42395 for nationwide findings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope specificity and supersession of prior findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparability findings can be issued for specific fishery IDs and can supersede previously published comparability findings for the same fisheries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Notice supersedes NMFS' previously published comparability findings for the listed fishery IDs (1883, 1968, 1969, 1977, 1978, 2041, 2046, 2047, 2051, 2052, 2053, 2054, 2064, 2067, and 2077). Other findings for different gear types or fishery IDs remain unaffected and valid.
